reply:
Ah. Right then. You're the one now.

I'm Rocco. I've had the rank out front for twenty years, kept on after Mickey, like. You'll want to know how things sit, I expect.

Twenty years I stood out there. Like I said. Since before you were... well, since a long time back anyway. Mickey kept me on and that was that, never saw reason to change it, and I never saw reason to leave. You know how it is.

Thirty-one years of them. You'll be the nephew, then.

Fish crate goes by, water off it right across my shoes and nobody so much as looks round. That's Tuesday for you, market or no market.

So listen, depends who you are and who owes you. The night crowd's different, there's the minicab rank on Copper Row if you know somebody there, the all-night place over the road does tea and the radio's always on. Or you walk. I walk. You see who's moving, who's stopped, what's changed since the morning. That's work for me, but it's something.

Well, that'd be three weeks now. Couple of the drivers came by to pay respects, you know how it goes. The woman from the flats over the road, she brought a card round. And the fella who handles the accounts, he came through Tuesday asking about how things stood.

Haven't seen the new owner before today, which is you, so that's sorted now. Nobody else has been poking about the yard that I've clocked, if that's what you're asking. I keep an eye on it, goes with the work.
Depends which books you mean. The one Rocco'll show you balances fine. It's meant to.

Yeah, well. Not everyone, I know who's where and what they're after, that's different. 

So listen, you're new enough that I'm not placing you yet. There's the fella runs the rank on Copper Row, he's all right if you're straight with him. The market crowd know each other back years. Mickey used to run the minicab office, he's gone now, three weeks, and there's the nephew supposed to be taking it but I haven't clapped eyes on him yet.

Who should you know depends on what you're after, doesn't it. What are you doing round here?

Ah, well that's the thing, boss. I don't know whose it is. Thursday nights it sits on the rank, same spot, engine off, nobody in it that I can see. Then it's gone by morning. Happened last week, happened the week before. Same van, same time.

Could be nothing. Could be somebody waiting for a fare that never shows, could be they're parked here and walking somewhere else. But I notice what parks on my rank, and that one's regular as clockwork now. You want me keeping a closer eye on it?
Mickey owed people plenty of things. Money's the one that gets written down. The rest you just carry.

So listen. Not to me they're not. I hear things, the rank talk, the market talk, but nobody's come asking me specific about the office. 

Why, someone should be asking questions about it?

You can count on me the same way Mickey did, boss. I mind the rank, I watch the gate, I see what comes and goes on this street. That hasn't changed.

Money's what changes things, though. I've always kept things proper when they're kept proper, if you follow me.
That's a bigger question than you've earned an answer to yet, new management. Ask me again when I've seen how you handle a Tuesday.
I don't know what you mean by that, mate. There's a place over the road does tea, there's the rank on Copper Row. What window? What happened?

They answer to you, I'd say. You own the place now. Though most of them haven't come round since Mickey went, so they might not know it yet. Word gets about, though, it always does on a street like this.

The ones who do show their faces, they'll figure it out quick enough when they see the name on the door.

I heard you the first time. Wanting a thing and being owed it aren't the same, and you're not owed it yet. Come back when the crate by the yard door's been moved and Rocco's stopped watching you sideways. Then we'll talk numbers.

I don't know who that is. And I don't ask about people I haven't heard of, that's how you stay out of trouble.

You asking about her for a reason, or just making conversation?

Depends, doesn't it. If it's somebody who's meant to be there, they come in the day and they show their face and we all know about it. That's normal.

If it's somebody who shouldn't be there, trying the gate after dark or moving quiet, well, I see them before they see the door, and then it's up to you what you want me to do about it. You want the door watched or you want it watched proper? Different money, friend.
Because thirty-one years doesn't just stop because a man does. Somebody's got to know what's true when the rest of them are busy deciding what's convenient. Right now that's me.

So listen, I'm always keeping my ears open, that's what I do. But you've got to tell me what I'm listening for, haven't you. Who is she, what's she after, why should I care? 

Because right now you're asking me to do something for nobody and that's not how it works.
Right you are, boss. I'll be out there same as always. You need me, you know where I am.
Morning's better. Crate might've moved by then. We'll see.
Yeah, all right. I'll be here, always am. You know where to find me.
Don't know a Victor, friend. You asking because somebody mentioned him, or are you just checking what I know?
Works the radio and the phone, back in the office. Sharper than she lets on. You'll meet her soon enough if you're sticking around.
